page: Amazon Web Services c6a.32xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. At its core is an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs utilizing simultaneous multithreading, capable of reaching clock frequencies up to 3.6 GHz on an x86_64 instruction set. Hardware security and cryptographic extensions include AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, alongside BMI2 and FMA instructions. The instance provides 256 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, delivering 2.0 GB per vCPU in line with traditional compute-heavy specifications. It features 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth but includes no integrated local NVMe storage and zero GPUs, requiring instances to depend on remote storage solutions for persistent data.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute and in-memory execution. The instance scores in the top 10% in multi-core stress testing, PassMark CPU tests, and encryption evaluations. Ray tracing performance in Geekbench ranks within the top decile, complemented by strong results in Clang software compilation and image processing. Memory throughput is substantial, yielding over 250 GB/s on large-block read operations and 124 GB/s on write operations. Furthermore, the instance attains exceptional throughput in in-memory key-value processing, logging 137.19 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations alongside strong static web serving capacity of 55.53 GB/s.

From a workload fit perspective, c6a.32xlarge offers high core density that maximizes CPU throughput relative to provisioned infrastructure overhead. However, the lack of local storage requires architectural consideration when designing I/O-intensive pipelines, as all disk traffic must route over the network. The 1:2 core-to-memory ratio also makes this instance suboptimal for memory-intensive in-memory databases with large footprints. Instead, it is well matched for scalable compute pipelines such as large-scale Clang code compilation, distributed video or ray tracing rendering, batch ETL data processing, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.32xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance engineered for compute-heavy, highly parallelized workloads. Powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 7R13 processors based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores running at up to 3.6 GHz. It is equipped with 256 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio typical of compute-focused platforms. The instance includes 50 Gbps of baseline networking capacity and contains no integrated local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage for persistence. In synthetic benchmarks, c6a.32xlarge achieves top-tier results in multi-core processing, PassMark CPU evaluation, ray tracing, and Redis throughput, while demonstrating strong memory bandwidth across uncached operations. Its high core density delivers efficient resource scaling for compute-bound tasks. This server profile is suited for distributed software compilation, batch processing, ray tracing, and high-throughput static web serving.
